title: Configured/default/no-op mutex method selection and lifecycle

scope.rationale: These functions select configured, pthread, or no-op mutex methods, publish allocation last across a memory barrier, invoke xMutexInit/xMutexEnd, and expose the profile concrete method tables.

dependencies.caller_closure: Default pthread, single-thread no-op, and configured method lifecycle paths are assigned through process/local Subsystem owners.

inputs: Core-mutex mode and optional copied sqlite3_mutex_methods before initialization
outputs: Initialized selected method owner or exact xMutexInit failure; matching xMutexEnd result at shutdown
contracts.ownership: Subsystem owns a copied method table; configured callback context/pointers remain configurator-owned. Process static native mutexes remain process-owned.
contracts.state_and_results: Configured methods take precedence. Otherwise core mode selects pthread and single-thread selects no-op. Allocation publication follows a full memory barrier. Failed xMutexInit leaves subsystem uninitialized.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: Invokes xMutexInit/xMutexEnd without holding a returned SQLite mutex. Sequentially consistent publication barriers protect method visibility. No I/O.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: Initialization callback failure propagates unchanged and permits reconfiguration/retry; end result propagates after state is cleared.

representation_differences: C copies nine callback fields into sqlite3GlobalConfig and publishes xMutexAlloc last; Zig copies the complete MutexMethods value into MethodsAdapter before sequentially consistent publication.
The GCC __sync_synchronize barrier is represented by a seq_cst atomic RMW barrier token.
Default concrete methods are direct native Subsystem operations instead of an ABI method-table roundtrip; configured methods retain callback transport exactly.

oracle.protocol: Infrastructure C/Zig differential compares copied configured method callbacks, init/end counts, allocation and enter/try/leave routing, single/multi/serialized mode transitions, 100 lifecycle cycles, and an eight-thread init race. Native Coordinator test proves configured methods provide allocator STATIC_MEM and public dynamic transport.
internal_observations: configured method copy survives caller mutation
configured STATIC_MEM used by memory Manager
oracle.normalization: Method-table/global addresses and barrier implementation bytes are ignored; callbacks, results, publication order, and lifecycle state are exact.

assurance.oom: No allocation by lifecycle itself; configured callback failure and dynamic mutex OOM are covered in dependencies.
assurance.io_crash_concurrency: No I/O. Publication uses seq_cst ordering and concurrent initialization is tested; formal weak-memory review remains open.
assurance.malformed_input: Missing configured callbacks remain a configuration precondition; default tables are complete.
assurance.continuation: Init failure/retry, repeated init, and idempotent shutdown are tested.
assurance.performance: Default path avoids callback indirection after selection; barrier count follows source publication boundaries.

integration.production_owner: src/core/mutex.zig Subsystem configured_methods and lifecycle methods
integration.native_call_path: global.process_coordinator starts selected mutex methods before memory and uses configured STATIC_MEM for Manager.lock; public mutex operations dispatch through the same process subsystem.
integration.bounded_owner_retired: Separate MethodsAdapter-only evidence is now integrated into Subsystem and production Coordinator lifecycle.

independent_review.notes: Must verify callback completeness/preconditions, publication ordering, failure retry, modes, and weak-memory semantics.

known_blockers: A typed process configuration function is exposed; consolidation into the final coherent configuration API domain remains open.
